I mean, there's a big difference in having a small business in Miller County versus downtown New York, what kind of a wage you'll pay. But I think, generally speaking, a minimum wage is something that is not helpful to small businesses because At the present time, their business model is built on a certain weight scale for their employees. And if you suddenly increase that significantly, they're going to have to make some choices, whether you retain employees by increasing your pay to them and then have to increase the cost of your product or servers you're giving, or do you let employees go and find an alternative downsize, for instance, or do you go find some way to automate? You go to the bank or a credit union, you borrow the money to pay the bills for six weeks so that you can get by. Then when you get back on your feet, what do you do? You pay it back. I don't have a problem with that. The problem that we have at the national level is borrowing the money to be able to get us through this problem.
